title: Advanced Critical Power Architecture
summary: Interpret a simplified critical-power path and its downstream dependencies in a simulation.
objectives: Trace utility, UPS, distribution, PDU, and server relationships.
Identify monitoring points, alternate sources, and dependencies without performing electrical work.

vocab.def: The modeled delivery of power from a source to downstream equipment.
A conceptual alternate route around a component during an authorized state.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This is a simulation-only learning activity. Do not open panels, operate switchgear, reset breakers, or handle energized equipment.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Accessible diagram equivalent: utility source connects to modeled switchgear, then UPS, distribution, rack PDU, and server. A backup source can feed the transfer concept. Monitoring points report source, UPS, distribution, and downstream states. Trace dependencies before making a reliability claim.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Document the observed path, alternate path, downstream impact, and uncertainty.

practice.prompt: What should a learner do when a power-path action is outside scope?
practice.answer: Stop, document the condition, and escalate to an authorized qualified role.

quiz.question: What is the safest use of a simplified power diagram?
options: Trace modeled dependencies and document uncertainty
quiz.answer: Trace modeled dependencies and document uncertainty

reflectionPrompt: Which power-path facts were directly supported by the model?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
